texts.preamble: Ram Charan Mahto vs State Of Jharkhand on 27 July, 2017 Author: Rongon Mukhopadhyay Bench: Rongon Mukhopadhyay In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi Cr. Rev. No. 235 of 2005 --- Ram Charan Mahto son of Aghnu Mahto Resident of Village Debadih, Police Station Sonahatu, District Ranchi ... ... Petitioner Versus State of Jharkhand ... ... Opp. Party --- Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay --- For the Petitioner : None
texts.facts: As the matter is pending since the year 2005 the same is being disposed of based on the material available on record. The prosecution story as would appear from the prosecution report is that 600 grams of Rahar Dal was taken from the shop of the petitioner on 29.10.1996 and the receipt was also granted in favour of the petitioner. The seized Rahar Dal was sealed in three packets each containing 200 grams and was sent to the public analyst for analysis. The report opined that sample of Rahar Dal contained coal tar (metanil yellow) and since the same was found to be adulterated, the prosecution report was filed under Section 16(1)(a)(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act against the petitioner which was registered as Case No. 22 II-B/98. In course of trial the prosecution had examined as many as three witnesses in support of its case. Ram Charan Mahto vs State Of Jharkhand on 27 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135484032/ 1 P.W. - 1, Mahendra Nath Sahu, is the Food Inspector who had stated that he had gone to the shop of the petitioner on 29.10.1996 along with one Siban Hazam and Vishwanath Singh Munda. He had stated that 600 grams of Rahar Dal was taken as sample which were kept in three packets containing 200 grams each and a receipt was also given to the petitioner. He had further stated that he had dispatched one sample to the public analyst through memorandum which was marked as Exhibit - 2. He had further stated that after obtaining the report of the public analyst he wrote a letter to the Civil surgeon, Ranchi for sanctioning of the prosecution and after obtaining the sanction the complaint was filed. P.W. - 2, Vishwanath Singh Munda, had stated that he was present when the sample of Rahar Dal was taken from the shop of the petitioner. P.W. - 3, Siban Hazam, had also supported the version of P.W. - 1 and P.W. - 2 and had stated that he was also present when the sample was taken and the receipt was granted in favour of the petitioner. Since the prosecution had been able to prove its case beyond all reasonable doubt the petitioner was convicted by the learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Khunti Ranchi in Case No. 22 II-B/98 on 04.08.2003 for the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for six months along with a fine of Rs. 1,000/-. The petitioner preferred an appeal being Criminal Appeal No. 91 of 2003 which however was dismissed by the learned Additional Judicial Commissioner, Fast Track Court, Khunti, Ranchi on 14.12.2004. The main plank of argument before the learned trial court on behalf of the petitioner was that proper compliance was not made with respect to Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
texts.arguments: Section 13 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 deals with the report of public analyst and sub-section (2) of Section 13 reads as follows:- " (2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory." Ram Charan Mahto vs State Of Jharkhand on 27 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135484032/ 2 Sub-section (2) of Section 13, therefore, clearly reveals that as soon as the report of the public analyst is made available a copy of the same has to be given to the person/persons who are aggrieved by the report of the public analyst so that they can make an application to the concerned court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of a copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food analyzed by the Central Food Laboratory.
